subject.title: Plugin installs crash Express 4.x routes: core npm-shrinkwrap pins path-to-regexp@8.x but no central override covers plugins

question: Should OpenClaw stop applying the full root workspace override set to third-party managed npm plugin projects, or keep that policy and only add diagnostics for Express 4/path-to-regexp conflicts?
rationale: Changing override propagation affects third-party plugin install compatibility and OpenClaw's security/reproducibility policy, so automation should not choose the permanent dependency-ownership boundary alone.

options.title: Scope propagated overrides
options.body: Filter or namespace root workspace overrides before applying them to third-party plugin projects, preserving only explicitly approved managed-root security pins and adding Express 4 regression proof.

options.title: Add validator only
options.body: Keep current override propagation but detect Express 4/path-to-regexp conflicts and fail with actionable reinstall or package-owner guidance.

options.title: Require plugin-owned fixes
options.body: Leave OpenClaw installer behavior unchanged and document that affected plugins must pin path-to-regexp or upgrade to Express 5, accepting current runtime failures in managed installs.

recommendation.title: Scope propagated overrides
recommendation.body: Filter or namespace root workspace overrides before applying them to third-party plugin projects, preserving only explicitly approved managed-root security pins and adding Express 4 regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The available local provenance points to this account on the central managed npm root and plugin install surfaces, despite shallow-history uncertainty.
